title: Efforts to Reduce Greenhouse Emissions by Industries in Singapore
what_it_is: Efforts to Reduce Greenhouse Emissions by Industries in Singapore

sections.label: Singapore fossil fuel imports and emissions
sections.summary: Singapore imported 190 Mtoe of fossil fuels in 2017, generated 52.5 million tonnes of greenhouse gases, and pledged under the Paris Agreement to cut emissions intensity by 36% from 2005 levels by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: In 2017, 190 million tonnes of oil equivalent (Mtoe) of fossil fuels were imported into Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: About 55 Mtoe were refined into higher value chemicals and fuels and mostly exported for use in other countries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Singapore generated 52.5 million tonnes of greenhouse gases in 2017, of which industries contribute about 60%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Around three-quarters of industries’ emissions are from the refining and petrochemicals sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Under the Paris Agreement, Singapore has pledged to reduce our emissions intensity by 36% from 2005 levels by 2030 and to reduce our total carbon emissions beyond 2030.

sections.label: Energy efficiency funding and management systems
sections.summary: From January 2019 funding support under EDB's REG(E) and NEA's E2F rose to 50% of qualifying costs, and from 2021 companies under the Energy Conservation Act must establish energy management systems.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: From January 2019, the funding support for the adoption of energy-efficient technologies under the Economic Development Board's (EDB’s) Resource Efficiency Grant for Energy (REG(E)) and the National Environment Agency's (NEA’s) Energy Efficiency Fund (E2F) has been increased from the previous cap of 30%, to 50% of the qualifying costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: From 2021 onwards, companies regulated under the Energy Conservation Act must establish energy management systems and regularly assess energy efficiency opportunities.

sections.label: Refinery expansion and Paris Agreement goals
sections.summary: The aim for expanded refineries is carbon and energy efficiency, and Singapore remains committed to cutting emissions intensity by 36% from 2005 levels, peaking in 2030 and reducing beyond.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But I would say that, in principle, when we expand the presence of our refineries here, whether it is a new and or an existing one, the aim is to ensure that they are carbon- and energy-efficient.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And let me also say that we are committed to our Paris Agreement goals that regardless of industry expansion of new plants, we want to make sure that we still cut our emissions intensity by 36% from 2005 levels and to peak in 2030, and to reduce beyond that.
